source.version: Undated 55-page preprint; the document prints no version number or date. The citation record identifies arXiv:2405.17924v1, submitted 2024-05-28; the local PDF SHA-256 matches the byte-verified version recorded there.
source.supplement_used: Appendix A (PDF pp. 34-36) and Appendix B (PDF pp. 37-55) in the saved PDF. No external OSF supplement or preregistration content was accessible.

studies.label: Experiment I (teams: human-only vs single-AI vs multiple-AI)
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Teams were randomized. The OLS analyses enter each team-task output as an observation and report robust standard errors, without stating clustering by team (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 2.1; PDF pp. 37-39, Appendix B, Tables 1-3). The Bayesian model also has no stated team random effect or cluster adjustment.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 2.1 (cohort); PDF p. 9, Section 2.1 (assignment); PDF p. 34, Appendix A, Table 1 (team counts)
counts_source.quote: 435 working professionals ... 142 participants were assigned to the human-only team, 150 to the single-AI team, and 143 to the multiple-AI team conditions. ... Human-Only Team (N=42) Single-AI Team (N=41) Multiple-AI Team (N=39)

arms.name: Human-only team
arms.description: Teams completed both tasks without AI. AI refinement offered after submission is explicitly excluded from the paper analysis (PDF p. 9, Section 2.1 and footnote 4).

arms.name: Single-AI team
arms.description: Teams completed both tasks with a single shared ChatGPT4.0 touchpoint (PDF p. 9, Section 2.1).

arms.name: Multiple-AI team
arms.description: Teams completed both tasks with as many ChatGPT4.0 touchpoints as team members (PDF p. 9, Section 2.1).

studies.task: Each team wrote a series of in-depth articles on college students’ job hunting and career development and developed a digital transformation strategy for a traditional retail chain.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT4.0
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 2.1; the model release year is not printed.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 4, footnote 1: https://osf.io/5su8c/?view_only=24f9efec395c4581b880e7773792d23d. Linked content could not be accessed.

studies.shared_sample: No other paper is identified as sharing participants in the screening form. Within this paper Experiment II reuses the Experiment I teams as comparators; whether its individual-AI participants previously joined Experiment I is unstated (PDF p. 11, Section 2.2; forms/c446.json, sample_overlap).

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Task outputs rated on a scale from one to ten by six independent online-panel judges, blind to hypotheses and treatment conditions; analysis uses a score per team-task output (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 2.1). The paper does not specify the rater-score aggregation formula.

regression.model: OLS; Human-only team is the reference. Controls are standardized team age, gender, education, IQ, previous AI use, size, and familiarity, with task fixed effects. Outcome is in original rating-scale units.

paper_effect.standardizer: Additional outcome variance explained by AI integration, reported in percent; no outcome-SD standardizer.

sources.quote: enhancement in overall quality when AI is utilized (β = 0.417, p < .01), explaining additional 3.7% variance in performance.

estimates.notes: The reported N counts team-task outputs, not people. Analyzed headcounts are not separately printed. The Total arm SDs are across outputs from both tasks, not across participants or team averages. Robust SEs are not stated to account for repeated outputs from the same randomized team. OLS confidence-interval endpoints are shown only graphically in Figures 3-4 and are not transcribed or derived. The paper does not print the combined AI arm mean or SD; the control arm descriptives are reported. paper_effect is the reported additional variance explained in percent, without conversion to a fraction or an SMD. Overall quality is coded usefulness under the codebook, not overall_creativity.

open_items: Exact analyzed people counts overall and by arm are not separately printed. Assignment headcounts must not be relabeled as analyzed counts, and output/cluster counts must not be relabeled as people.
The paper reports output-level robust OLS SEs without stating team clustering. Team-level precision, or data permitting estimation at the randomized-team level, is needed for pooling.
For the both-task outcomes, no SD across team-average scores or participant-level SD is printed; the descriptive SDs are across team-task outputs.

The combined AI arm has no printed mean or SD. Task-specific tests, contrast uncertainty, and separate task-specific output counts are not printed. No means, SDs, Ns, effects, or intervals were derived.
The Bayesian posterior means and intervals in Section 3.2.2 conflict with Appendix B Table 4. Both printed versions are retained as dependent analysis variants; author clarification is needed.

The named external OSF supplement and preregistration, including attempted OSF API alternatives, were inaccessible through Python urllib because of WinError 10013. Additional supplementary statistics and preregistered outcome priority remain unverified.
The country of participant recruitment and the AI model release year are not explicitly stated. Country is not inferred from author affiliation, and the model year is null.
The task-output rating aggregation formula is not explicitly described, although the paper states that each output was assessed by six raters and analyzes one score per team-task output.
The citation record identifies the saved arXiv version but cannot establish whether a later SSRN revision exists. The document itself prints no date or version number.
Whether the Experiment II individual-AI participants had previously participated in Experiment I is unstated. Experiment II is excluded, and no cross-experiment unique-person total is asserted.
notes: Extraction B, 2026-10-11. The full markdown conversion was read in contiguous chunks through the end of Appendix B. PDF tables, figure pages, appendices, and every cited numerical page were checked with pymupdf; figure images were rendered only in memory. The saved PDF matches the SHA-256 recorded in forms/citations/c446.json. PDF pages are one-based; the main-text printed page numbers coincide with PDF pages, while the figure and appendix pages have no numerical printed pagination. Statistic inventory: Appendix A Table 1 prints arm means and output-level SDs for each performance dimension over both tasks and separately by task. Appendix B Tables 1-3 print the eligible full-sample OLS coefficients, robust SEs, output Ns, and significance markers. Section 3.2.1 reports additional variance explained in percent. Appendix B Table 4 prints Bayesian posterior means, posterior SDs, credible intervals, and inverse Bayes factors; Section 3.2.2 prints conflicting Bayesian means and intervals. All these treatment-contrast statistics are preserved, with posterior SDs retained in notes and their verbatim row quotes because the schema has no posterior-SD field. Bayesian records are alternative analyses of the same contrast, not additional samples. Model-fit diagnostics, intercepts, and covariate slopes are not treatment-effect estimates. Task-specific descriptive rows represent the full assigned arms on each task and are retained in addition to the pooled-task model; the tasks combine creative writing and strategy ideation, so the study-level task_type is other. Overall quality is coded usefulness as specified in the codebook. Only with_ai outcomes are reported. Relative rating-score distributions are not across_people content diversity. Post-submission AI refinement in the human-only arm is explicitly excluded from the paper analysis (PDF p. 9, footnote 4), and no after_ai output is reported. The only file written is extraction/raw/c446.B.json. No effect-size calculation, inferred headcount, pooled descriptive statistic, graphical digitization, or posterior-SD-to-SE substitution was performed.
